questions.question_text: State two ways to increase the magnetic strength of an electromagnet.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Increase the magnitude of electric current by adding more cells. 2. Increase the number of wire turns wrapped around the iron core.

questions.question_text: Explain why nichrome wire is used in heating elements of electric irons, whereas copper wire is used for connecting leads.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Nichrome has high electrical resistance and a high melting point, converting electrical energy into high thermal heat without melting. Copper has very low resistance, allowing current to flow with minimal energy loss or heating.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study Questions)

questions.question_text: Describe an experiment to test electrical conduction in liquids using an LED circuit, and contrast tap water with distilled water.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Setup: Connect a 3V battery cell in series with an LED and two open wire test leads. 2. Testing Distilled Water: Submerge leads into pure distilled water; the LED does not glow because distilled water lacks free mobile ions required to carry electric charge. 3. Testing Tap Water: Submerge leads into tap water; the LED glows dimly because dissolved mineral salts dissociate into mobile ions. 4. Conclusion: Liquids conduct electricity through mobile ion movement.

questions.question_text: Why is a thin nichrome wire used in heating appliances like room heaters?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Nichrome wire has high electrical resistance and high melting point. When current flows, high resistance converts electrical energy efficiently into intense thermal heat without melting.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 4.2 Heating Effect and Liquid Conduction and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Electrical resistance converts electrical energy into heat in high-resistance conductors (Nichrome). Electric fuses contain low-melting-point alloy wires that melt during current overload. Liquids containing dissolved ions conduct current. [Safety Note: Electric Fuse Wire] Never replace a blown fuse wire with copper wire, as copper's high melting point prevents safety shutdown during overload.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 4.1 Magnetic Effect of Current and Electromagnets and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Flowing electric current creates a surrounding magnetic field (Oersted, 1820). Wrapping insulated copper wire around a soft iron nail creates an electromagnet whose strength increases with current magnitude and coil turn density. [Historical Note: Oersted's Discovery] Hans Christian Oersted noticed a compass needle twitch when an electric current was switched on nearby.

questions.question_text: Explain the working mechanism of an electric fuse and why copper wire should never replace fuse wire.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An electric fuse contains an alloy wire with a low melting point calibrated to melt if current exceeds safe limits. Copper has a high melting point and high current capacity; using copper prevents the fuse from melting during an overload, risking electrical fire.
